name: Tricentis
tagline: Enterprise test automation and quality management suite: Tosca for model-based UI and API testing, qTest for test management, NeoLoad for load testing.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Tricentis sells through enterprise quotes and does not publish list pricing.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely one-shot a test runner. What you cannot one-shot is Tosca's model-based test design against SAP, Salesforce, Oracle, mainframe green screens and a dozen other packaged apps whose UIs change every quarter under someone else's release schedule. The paid product exists so that a QA team of non-programmers can maintain thousands of regression cases, and so that an auditor can be handed a signed report showing which requirement was covered by which run. A personal build gives you Playwright with nicer reporting, which is fine, but nobody was paying Tricentis for a test runner. If your actual need is 'run my own browser tests and see a report', build that and never look at this category again.
coreLoopDIY: A local Playwright suite with reusable page modules, a YAML-defined test-case layer so cases can be edited without touching code, and a self-contained HTML report with history.
requirements: Test targets you actually control or are allowed to automate
whatYouLose: Model-based test design: prebuilt, vendor-maintained modules for SAP, Salesforce, Oracle EBS, SAP GUI and mainframe terminals
Non-coder authoring, so QA analysts can build and maintain cases without touching a repo
Test management and traceability: requirements coverage, audit trails, sign-off, the artifacts regulated industries get asked for
Load and performance testing at realistic scale, plus the infra to generate it
Support contracts, SLAs and someone to blame when a release ships broken
moatNotes: The SAP relationship is the load-bearing wall. Tricentis maintains automation modules against packaged enterprise apps that change on the vendor's timetable, not yours.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the buyer is not a developer. Large organizations have thousands of regression cases covering ERP processes that touch finance, and those cases are authored and maintained by QA analysts who do not write code and should not have to. Tricentis sells the authoring layer, the vendor-maintained connectors to packaged apps, and the paper trail that satisfies an audit. Ripping that out and replacing it with a repo of Playwright specs means retraining a department and rebuilding years of accumulated test assets, which is exactly why nobody does it.
notes: A test runner is a weekend; a maintained automation layer for SAP is not. The moat is vendor-maintained connectors to packaged enterprise apps plus the audit trail that makes the QA department defensible.
prompt:
Build a local browser regression testing harness. No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Node.js 20+, TypeScript, Playwright Test as the runner
- Zod for config validation
- No database: results are JSON files on disk

Structure:
- /modules: reusable page modules. Each exports named actions like login(page, user), openInvoice(page, id). Selectors live only here, never in test cases.
- /cases: test cases as YAML files. A case has: name, tags, and a list of steps. Each step is { module, action, args }. Optional expect blocks with { selector, state: visible|hidden|text, value }.
- /src/loader.ts: reads YAML cases, validates with Zod, resolves module.action references, produces Playwright tests dynamically.
- /src/report.ts: after each run, write results to /runs/RUN_ID.json and regenerate /runs/index.html.

The report page is a single self-contained HTML file: no CDN, inline CSS and JS. Show a table of cases with pass/fail/skip, duration, tags, and last 10 runs as a pass/fail strip per case so flaky cases stand out. Clicking a failed case shows the failing step, the error, and a link to the screenshot Playwright saved.

Requirements:
- Playwright config: retries 1, trace and screenshot on first retry, HTML artifacts under /artifacts.
- Base URL and credentials come from .env, read via process.env, never committed. Ship a .env.example.
- CLI: npm run test, npm run test -- --grep-tag smoke, npm run report to open the latest report.
- Ship two example modules and three example YAML cases against a public demo site so the repo runs green on first clone.

Explicitly out of scope: no visual diffing, no load testing, no SAP or Salesforce connectors, no multi-user auth, no requirements traceability, no CI config beyond a single GitHub Actions workflow that runs the suite on push.

Write a README that states plainly what this does not do.
